agency_full: European Space Agency (lead) — DLR (Philae lander) / CNES / ASI / NASA (DSN tracking + 3 instruments)
payload: Orbiter (~2900 kg dry, 11 instruments) + Philae descent lander (~100 kg, 10 instruments). Heatshield, two Earth + one Mars gravity assist, 957 days of deep-space hibernation 2011–2014.
credit: © ESA / Rosetta / NavCam / OSIRIS — CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO mission imagery. Rosetta launched 2004-03-02 from Kourou on a 10-year cruise that included Earth gravity assists (2005-03-04, 2007-11-13, 2009-11-13) and a Mars flyby (2007-02-25), with main-belt asteroid encounters at 2867 Šteins (2008-09-05) and 21 Lutetia (2010-07-10). The spacecraft hibernated 2011-06 to 2014-01 (deep-space radio silence, beyond solar-array operating range), then woke and rendezvoused with comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko 2014-08-06 — the first spacecraft ever to enter orbit around a comet. Philae detached 2014-11-12 and bounced into the shadow of a cliff after harpoon failure; it returned ~60 hours of science before its primary battery drained. Rosetta itself observed 67P through perihelion (2015-08-13) and into outbound dust decay before a controlled descent to the surface on 2016-09-30 ended the mission. Key discoveries: organics + glycine + phosphorus in comet coma; deuterium-to-hydrogen ratio that ruled out Jupiter-family comets as Earth's primary water source; first close-up imaging of cometary outgassing geometry.

events.label: Launch — Ariane 5 G+
events.description: Kourou, French Guiana, 2004-03-02. ESA's flagship cometary mission, designed to rendezvous with comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko during its 2014–2016 inner-solar-system passage. The launch slipped 13 months from a January 2003 window targeting comet 46P/Wirtanen — a fault in Ariane 5 forced re-planning to the alternative comet.

events.label: Earth #1 — gravity assist
events.description: Closest approach 1,955 km on 2005-03-04. First of four gravity assists in the cruise plan — the chemical engine alone can't reach 67P's aphelion at 5.7 AU.

events.label: Mars — gravity assist
events.description: Closest approach 250 km above the Martian surface on 2007-02-25 — only 15 minutes inside Mars's eclipse. The spacecraft was put into hibernation mode during the brief eclipse to conserve power, then commanded back to operation immediately on emergence.

events.label: Earth #2 — gravity assist
events.description: Closest approach 5,295 km on 2007-11-13. Briefly mistaken for a near-Earth asteroid (designated 2007 VN84) before observers realised it was Rosetta heading out.

events.label: Steins (2867) — asteroid flyby
events.description: Closest approach 800 km from main-belt asteroid 2867 Steins on 2008-09-05. Steins's diamond-shaped 6 km E-type body provided the first close-up confirmation of an enstatite-chondrite parent body's surface morphology.

events.label: Earth #3 — gravity assist
events.description: Final Earth flyby on 2009-11-13, closest approach 2,481 km. The boost takes Rosetta out to the aphelion needed to match 67P's orbit, after which the spacecraft entered deep-space hibernation.

events.label: Lutetia (21) — asteroid flyby
events.description: Closest approach 3,168 km from main-belt asteroid 21 Lutetia on 2010-07-10. At 100 km diameter, Lutetia is the largest asteroid ever visited at close range; the M-type spectrum + high density suggested a metal-rich differentiated body.

events.label: 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko rendezvous + Philae landing
events.description: Arrived at comet 67P on 2014-08-06 — the first spacecraft to rendezvous with a comet (matching velocities, not just flying past). Released Philae lander on 2014-11-12; Philae bounced twice in the comet's ~10⁻⁴ g gravity but returned 64 hours of surface data. Rosetta continued orbiting 67P through perihelion in 2015, ended on 2016-09-30 with a controlled descent to the comet's surface.
